Natural: The sugary drinks portion cap rule, also known as the soda ban, was a proposed limit on soft drink size in New York City, intended to prohibit the sale of sweetened drinks larger than 16 fluid ounces. The rule was strongly supported by Mayor Michael Bloomberg and his successor, Mayor Bill de Blasio, but was opposed by beverage companies and some community groups. The rule was ultimately repealed by the New York Court of Appeals in 2014, citing that the New York City Board of Health exceeded its regulatory authority.
